A2UI Catalog / surfaces / android

Android

Android, through Google's A2UI renderer. Google's androidx.a2ui library renders A2UI natively in Jetpack Compose. Add the atomic-catalog library and an Android app can show every atom listed here: Basic Catalog components draw in Compose, and the rest draw with this catalog's own renderer inside the app. Apps without the library still get something useful: the catalog's emitter reads which catalogs an app supports and sends a plain Basic Catalog version instead of a surface the app can't draw.

val catalog = A2uiAtomicCatalog.catalog(context)

Build it from source for now; a published package is coming. Source and README · tested on a Pixel 7 Pro with androidx.a2ui 1.0.0-alpha01.

563 catalog atoms also render on this surface

                  Concept explainer · the renderer

                  How the A2UI Renderer Works: JSON In, HTML Out

                  One dispatch function, one renderer per type — that's the whole engine.

                  You pick a component from the catalog. You write a JSON payload. A rendered page appears — styled, interactive, surface-appropriate. No HTML written. No CSS authored.

                  The model

                  The renderer is a translator: JSON in, HTML out. The schema is the *what* (vocabulary), the renderer is the *how* (implementation).

                  Swap the renderer file, keep the payload, get a different surface — the JSON is the contract; the renderer is the adapter.

                  1
                  DEPTH 1

                  The contract: one function per type

                  The schema defines every component type and its fields — stat_card has value, label, delta. For every type in the catalog there is exactly one renderer function that takes a block and returns HTML.

                  _RENDERERS['stat_card'] = function(b) {
  return '<div class="stat-card">'
    + '<div class="value">' + b.value + '</div>'
    + '</div>';
};
                  >Every component — from a body block to an interactive globe — is one entry in _RENDERERS.
                  2
                  DEPTH 2

                  The adapter: same payload, different surface

                  A stat_card payload is identical on Apps Script web, a Meet stage sidebar, or a web article. What changes is the renderer — each surface ships its own implementation tuned for that environment.

                  EX
                  WORKED EXAMPLE

                  The extreme case: globe_3d

                  Twelve lines of JSON produce a self-contained interactive 3-D globe — draggable with inertia, dot pins at lat/lon, great-circle arcs. ~160 lines of renderer code, zero external libraries, CSP-safe.

                  {
  "type": "globe_3d",
  "theme": "earth",
  "size": 400,
  "dots": [
    {"lat": 48.8, "lon": 2.3, "label": "Paris"},
    {"lat": 40.7, "lon": -74, "label": "NYC"}
  ]
}

                  The developer writes the JSON. The renderer handles the rest.

                  Concept Rung

                  one depth level (kind chip, title, body, code, takeaway) — normally used inside concept_ladder

                  DEPTH 2

                  The adapter: same payload, different surface

                  A stat_card payload is identical across surfaces. What changes is the renderer — each surface ships its own implementation of the same contract.
